facts.label: Liquidity adequacy
facts.text: Liquidity at October 2, 2026 was cash of USD 188,648 thousand plus USD 760 million of revolver availability, which equals the USD 1,050 million facility less USD 290 million drawn and is available only while financial covenants are met. Of the cash, USD 176.5 million sat outside the United States, where repatriation can bear withholding taxes and minority-owner restrictions, so the usable domestic cash is small. Debt due within a year is USD 9,357 thousand, the nearest large maturities are the notes due April 2029 and the term loan and revolver due October 2030, and the revolver carries a springing maturity whose trigger the filing does not describe. Letters of credit of USD 53.6 million are outstanding under separate facilities with USD 116.8 million of capacity. The consequence is ample near-term liquidity but a dependence on the revolver, whose covenants cannot be tested from the filings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C7

facts.text: Three definitions need care. First, ESAB states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA here is operating income plus the cash flow statement's depreciation, amortization and other impairment charges, and it sits USD 123.606 million below the issuer's last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 589.7 million; the gap is restructuring, acquisition and integration costs, inventory step-up and a non-cash option award that the issuer adds back, and the reported measure is the primary denominator here with the adjusted measure shown beside it. Third, the 2025 annual report re-presents the FY2024 cash flow statement, splitting the gain on sale of property from other operating items and issuance costs from other financing, with unchanged totals; the FY2024 column here uses the later presentation. Action: obtain cash paid for interest for the nine months of 2026 or state cover on interest expense with that definition labelled. - The legal rank and security of the term loan and revolver, and their rank against the senior notes, are not stated, so no debt stack is drawn and the instrument register shows security and ranking as not supplied for those facilities. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement and indentures. - Cash flow statements are year-to-date only, so discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows and the fourth quarter of 2025 are not reported; Q4 2025 net sales are derived by difference, the second-quarter income columns are not tabulated because they are carried in the six-month columns, and cash flows by quarter would be derived and labelled. Severity: Low. Action: derive and label when a quarterly view is needed. - Per-share lines, the statement of comprehensive income and the statement of equity are not tabulated, and the FY2023 and FY2022 columns of the annual reports are not carried; they do not affect leverage, cover or liquidity. Severity: Low. Action: extend the tables if earnings per share or a longer history is needed. - Instrument carrying values are not disclosed, the other debt line of 7041 thousand is not described, and no floor or amortisation schedule is stated for the term loan after 2026. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement; meanwhile the register carries principal and one financing cost adjustment row. - Several statement lines print a dash for a period (pension settlement loss, preferred stock proceeds and dividends, term loan lines, Senior Notes proceeds); each is recorded as not supplied rather than as zero. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the credit view. - No operating KPIs such as orders, backlog or volumes are stated beyond the issuer's margins and sales growth components. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a volume view is wanted. - The Q1 2026 balance sheet holds cash raised ahead of the Eddyfi closing, so its net debt is not comparable with year-end 2025 or the later dates; it is shown with that label and not treated as a leverage reading. Severity: Low. Action: none; read the July 3 and October 2, 2026 rows as the first post-closing figures.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a moderate governance rating is the pace and direction of financial policy: ESAB bought four businesses in 2025 and a USD 1.5 billion business in 2026, raised its dividend as the deal closed, and granted management options that pay only on a much higher share price, all while its finance leadership changed and one acquired unit's controls were still being brought into scope at the end of 2025. Insider participation in the preferred stock can also be read the other way, since the Rales-affiliated buyers took a 6.50% cumulative claim that ranks ahead of common equity and the placement terms were negotiated with the unaffiliated investors rather than set by the company alone. The view would move to high if a further large acquisition were funded mainly with debt before leverage falls, if the dividend rose again, or if the missing proxy statement showed a small board majority tied to the Rales Holders. It would move to low if the proxy statement showed an independent board and no concentrated holder, the credit agreement showed distribution limits that bind, and the reason for the finance leadership change proved routine. citations.quote: The strongest evidence against a moderate governance rating is the pace and direction of financial policy: ESAB bought four businesses in 2025 and a USD 1.5 billion business in 2026, raised its dividend as the deal closed, and granted management options that pay only on a much higher share price, all while its finance leadership changed and one acquired unit's controls were still being brought into scope at the end of 2025. Insider participation in the preferred stock can also be read the other way, since the Rales-affiliated buyers took a 6.50% cumulative claim that ranks ahead of common equity and the placement terms were negotiated with the unaffiliated investors rather than set by the company alone. The view would move to high if a further large acquisition were funded mainly with debt before leverage falls, if the dividend rose again, or if the missing proxy statement showed a small board majority tied to the Rales Holders. It would move to low if the proxy statement showed an independent board and no concentrated holder, the credit agreement showed distribution limits that bind, and the reason for the finance leadership change proved routine.

facts.label: T2D.9 Sponsor Risk Assessment
facts.text: The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium. It is driven by a part-equity, mostly debt-funded acquisition and a raised dividend, because those choices add fixed charges and leave less room for a second deal, which implies higher refinancing exposure until earnings absorb Eddyfi. Countervailing evidence is the insider equity support, the absence of a sponsor and of any documented extraction, and the unused buyback. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: ESAB's fundamental credit profile is adequate but stretched by acquisition debt, with total debt at 5.00x reported and 3.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, so creditors rely on integration and cash flow, not balance-sheet cushion, until leverage falls. Cash of USD 188,648 thousand (pro forma cash is not established), USD 760 million undrawn on the revolver, no large maturity before April 2029 and consumables at 60.96% of nine-month sales are the main supports; an estimated interest cover of 3.69x, down from 7.46x in FY2025, a raised dividend and finance leadership turnover are the main constraints. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation B1; calculation B8; calculation B9

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - The business profile is the strongest dimension. Consumables were 60.96% of nine-month net sales, about 80% of FY2025 sales came from outside the United States, and sales split 39.60% Americas and 60.40% EMEA & APAC, so no region or product group dominates; issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 19.03% of last-twelve-months net sales. The consequence is revenue that is recurring and spread, which supports cash flow through a downturn better than a project-driven equipment business would. facts.text: - Leverage is the weakest dimension and is driven by the acquisition. Total debt is 5.00x reported and 3.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA at October 2, 2026, against 2.49x and 2.21x at year-end 2025, which is before Eddyfi, so a pro forma year-end 2025 figure is not established. Last-twelve-months EBITDA holds only about 4 months of Eddyfi, so the run-rate ratio is lower than these figures, but the filings do not say by how much. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Liquidity is adequate and maturities are back-ended. Cash is USD 188,648 thousand and USD 760 million of the USD 1,050 million revolver is undrawn, with 27.62% drawn; the first large maturity is USD 700 million of senior notes in April 2029, followed by the term loan and revolver in October 2030 and USD 1,000 million of notes in April 2031, so the two bonds are 72.43% of principal. Pro forma cash for the October 2026 dividends is not established. The consequence is no refinancing pressure for more than two years, but a concentrated wall from 2029 to 2031 that needs market access. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; calculation B7; calculation B8

facts.text: - Cash generation is positive but thin against the debt. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Interest cost is the main step-up and cover will fall. Cash interest paid was USD 66,569 thousand in FY2025 for cover of 7.46x on reported EBITDA, but the larger debt at a weighted-average rate of 5.40% implies roughly USD 126,360 thousand a year, an estimated cover of 3.69x on reported EBITDA and 4.67x on adjusted EBITDA. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that leverage is less of a concern than it looks is that the debt is fully loaded but the earnings are not: last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 589.7 million holds only about 4 months of Eddyfi, whose 2025 revenue of about USD 240 million was 8.44% of ESAB's net sales, so a full year would lift EBITDA and lower leverage, and liquidity of USD 760 million undrawn plus cash gives time. The case that it is worse than it looks is that reported EBITDA is USD 466,094 thousand, well below the adjusted figure, because restructuring and acquisition costs are real cash, and that the estimate of cover at 3.69x leaves little room if earnings slip. The view would improve if a pro forma EBITDA showed total leverage below 4x, if cash flow after capital spending rose above 10% of debt, or if the credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would worsen if reported EBITDA fell again, if the dividend rose or another large acquisition were debt-funded before leverage falls, or if the unexplained finance leadership change proved a sign of control problems. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation B4; calculation B9

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. A global, diversified, consumables-led business with about 80% of sales outside the United States and no customer above 10% of trade receivables turns volume into recurring cash flow, which supports debt service through a cycle. Liquidity of cash plus an undrawn USD 1,050 million revolver covers near-term needs, and nothing large matures before April 2029. Insiders and institutions put in USD 318 million of equity, which limited the debt added. The cash flow chain is evidence from the revenue and debt notes, the mechanism of recurring revenue and a back-ended maturity profile, and the implication of lower refinancing and default risk in the next two years. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Debt has roughly doubled to 5.00x reported EBITDA against 2.49x at year-end 2025, interest cost will take a much larger share of EBITDA, cash flow after capital spending is only 7.76% of debt, and a dividend raise, option awards tied to share prices and unexplained finance leadership changes point to a policy that favours growth over repair. The mechanism is higher fixed charges and slower deleveraging, and the implication is greater sensitivity of default and refinancing risk to an earnings miss during the integration year. facts.label: Company description and ownership
facts.text: ESAB makes welding and cutting systems, consumables, gas control equipment, automation and robotics, software and, since June 2026, advanced inspection technology, selling through distributors and direct sales in about 150 countries. Consumables are the larger and steadier part of sales, equipment the cyclical part, and acquisitions are a core strategy: four in 2025 and Eddyfi in 2026. The credit linkage is that recurring consumables and global spread support cash flow and refinancing confidence, while a strategy built on acquisitions means leverage will recur as a risk unless funding stays equity-light. ESAB is a listed company without a sponsor; Mitchell P. Rales is Executive Chair and the Rales Holders hold registration rights, but their percentage is not stated, so ownership concentration and distribution behaviour are rated on actions, not structure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 23

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Consumables, which are replaced as they are used, were 65.81% of FY2025 sales and 60.96% of nine-month 2026 sales, so volume follows industrial activity but with a floor from maintenance and replacement demand. Pricing has helped: Americas net sales from existing businesses rose on USD 25.2 million of customer pricing in the nine months while volumes fell in South America and Mexico, and EMEA & APAC organic growth was supported by pricing and Asia volumes against Middle East weakness. Organic growth was 0.9% in the nine months after minus 1.1% in FY2025, so revenue is stable rather than growing and acquisitions supply most of the growth; the credit implication is steady but not expanding cash flow that cannot by itself deleverage quickly. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Steel, iron, copper and aluminum are the main inputs, tariffs added cost from April 2025, and gross margin fell from 37.9% in FY2024 to 36.9% in FY2025 before recovering to 38.1% in the nine months of 2026 as pricing, favourable tariff effects and acquisitions helped. Operating income margin fell as selling and administrative costs and restructuring rose with the larger group, so the issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.8% for nine months is below 19.7% for FY2025. Margins can be defended through pricing, as 2026 shows, but integration and restructuring costs are cash, so reported EBITDA is the better measure of what services debt. facts.label: Capital intensity and FCF conversion
facts.text: Capital spending is modest at USD 49,700 thousand in nine months of 2026, though it rose from USD 27,654 thousand, and the issuer separates asbestos and restructuring cash from capital spending. Conversion of reported EBITDA to cash flow after capital spending was 38.78% over the last twelve months, held down by restructuring, integration, working capital and interest, and cash taxes and interest were substantial. The implication is that EBITDA overstates what is available for debt service, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA rising and cash costs falling, not on capital spending cuts. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5

facts.label: Market frameworks, credit-translated
facts.text: Rivalry is the force that matters: the filing names Lincoln Electric and the welding business of Illinois Tool Works as competitors and describes a fragmented market where price, quality and delivery decide, which caps pricing power and implies margins are defended by brands and aftermarket support rather than by dominance. Buyer power is limited by a diversified customer base with no customer above 10% of receivables, supplier power by multiple sources for steel, copper and aluminum, and entry and substitution threats are low in consumables and rising in automation, where the company itself invests in software and robotics. Macro, tariff and war factors are material enough for a PEST view: US tariffs raised costs and prices, IEEPA tariff refunds are not yet recorded as receivables, the Middle East conflict cut sales, and sanctions leave about USD 51 million of Russian cash hard to withdraw; the credit consequence is cost and cash volatility that the company has so far passed through to prices. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: On a ratings-style lens the assessments are as follows. Scale and market position are strong, and competitive advantage and business diversification average to strong given brands, aftermarket and geographic spread. Cost and capex flexibility and margin stability are average: pricing has defended margins but restructuring and integration costs are high. Free cash flow stability is average to weak because conversion is below 40% of reported EBITDA and falling interest cover will bite. Ability to refinance is average, helped by a back-ended wall and equity support but limited by leverage near 5x reported and unknown covenants. Liquidity is average to strong on cash and an undrawn revolver subject to covenants, and financial policy and governance are average because supportive equity funding is offset by a raised dividend, option incentives and turnover. The trend is deterioration in 2026 from the acquisition, with the main missing datapoints being covenant levels, pro forma EBITDA and interest paid. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B5

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are a full year of Eddyfi, pricing, tariff refunds and margin programmes; the headwinds are a high interest bill, continuing restructuring and integration cash costs, weak South American, Mexican and Middle East volumes, and the refinancing step at the 2029 notes. Over three to five years the maturity wall of 2029 to 2031 is the dominant issue and depends on leverage having fallen by then; the structural tailwind is automation, inspection and high-growth markets, which the issuer puts at 52% of FY2025 revenue by its own definition. No management guidance was supplied, so the outlook is qualitative. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with softer industrial demand and tariff-driven pricing fatigue during the first full year after the deal, the first operational break being lower consumables volumes and integration costs that run longer than planned. Reported EBITDA, already USD 466,094 thousand over twelve months, would fall, working capital would absorb cash again as in the nine months of 2026, and cash flow after capital spending, now USD 180,737 thousand, would approach the cash dividends and fixed charges. Liquidity of cash and USD 760 million undrawn would still cover near-term needs, but leverage would rise further and covenant headroom, which is not disclosed, becomes the observable trigger: a tightening revolver would leave the 2029 notes to be refinanced from a weaker position. Management levers are the dividend, capital spending, restructuring and asset sales; the evidence supports resilience sufficient to avoid distress in the next two years but not a comfortable deleveraging path. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B7

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, ESAB presents a solid business profile supported by scale, a consumables-led and geographically spread revenue base and insider equity support, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition leverage, a much higher interest burden and thin cash flow against debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to recurring consumables and pricing, but conversion is held down by integration and restructuring cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on deleveraging before the 2029 notes, on covenant headroom in the revolver and on market access. The primary downside path is an earnings or working-capital shortfall during integration. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, covenant terms, interest paid and management guidance. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: acquisition leverage with an undisclosed covenant backstop. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied SEC filings support the requested credit work on ESAB Corp, but only with limitations: leverage cannot be read directly because no pro forma or covenant-defined EBITDA is printed for the balance sheet enlarged by the June 2026 Eddyfi acquisition. Any leverage or covenant-headroom conclusion built on these filings should be labelled provisional until the credit agreement and a pro forma EBITDA are obtained.

The latest balance sheet is dated October 2, 2026, 47 days before the as-of date, and the annual and quarterly statements tie to one another on every amount tested. The acquisition breaks comparability, so year-end 2025 debt and cash predate it and should not be carried forward as current. No executed agreement, indenture, credit rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so legal, ratings and valuation work stays blocked.

# CP-1 Financial foundation: ESAB Corp (esab-1877322)
## Request

ESAB Corp (esab-1877322), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the financial foundation for ESAB Corporation from its FY2024 and FY2025 annual reports and its first three 2026 quarterly reports, in US dollars.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage roughly doubled with the June 2026 Eddyfi acquisition: total debt to reported EBITDA is 5.00x at the latest balance sheet against 2.49x at year-end 2025, and the 5.00x overstates the run-rate burden. The debt is fully loaded while last-twelve-months EBITDA holds only about 4 months of Eddyfi, so creditors should treat 3.95x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA as the better guide until pro forma EBITDA is disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; calculation C3; calculation C4

Liquidity is adequate at the latest date: cash of USD 188,648 thousand and USD 760 million undrawn on the revolver, against USD 9,357 thousand of debt due within a year. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 153,017 thousand covered little of the USD 1,469,372 thousand acquisition outflow, which was financed with new debt and equity. Covenant headroom and pro forma leverage are not calculable from the filings.
### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Total debt at carrying value rose from USD 1,234,952 thousand at year-end 2025 to USD 2,329,069 thousand at October 2, 2026, because ESAB issued USD 1,000,000 thousand of senior notes due 2031, drew on the revolver and paid USD 1,469,372 thousand for acquisitions. Net debt rose from USD 1,049,089 thousand to USD 2,140,421 thousand, so net debt to reported EBITDA moved from 2.11x to 4.59x and, on issuer-adjusted EBITDA, from 1.87x to 3.63x. Reported EBITDA for the last twelve months, USD 466,094 thousand, is below FY2025's USD 496,275 thousand, partly because nine-month restructuring charges of USD 39,807 thousand compare with USD 10,236 thousand a year earlier and acquisition costs and inventory step-up sit inside operating income, while the issuer adds them back to reach USD 589.7 million of Adjusted EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

The interim ratios show the path. At April 3, 2026 gross leverage was 4.21x but net leverage only 2.13x because the proceeds of the USD 1,000,000 thousand notes issue, less a USD 240 million revolver paydown, sat in cash of USD 1,004,790 thousand; at July 3, 2026, after the closing, net leverage was 4.72x. The creditor consequence is that the net figure at April 3, 2026 is not a leverage reading at all, and the first clean post-closing reading is July 3, 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-04-03_esab-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C3; calculation C4
### Coverage and cash-flow quality

Cash interest paid was USD 66,569 thousand in FY2025 and USD 62,280 thousand in FY2024, giving reported EBITDA cover of 7.46x and 8.26x. The quarterly reports print no cash interest paid, so cover after the 2026 financing cannot be computed; the income statement line for interest expense and other, net, which is not the same measure, rose from USD 23,584 thousand in Q3 2025 to USD 36,511 thousand in Q3 2026, so cover is likely to fall from the FY2025 level before Eddyfi earnings are fully in the base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5

Operating cash flow was USD 153,017 thousand in the nine months of 2026 against USD 163,514 thousand a year earlier, with purchases of property, plant and equipment of USD 49,700 thousand against USD 27,654 thousand, so cash flow after capital expenditure fell to USD 103,317 thousand from USD 135,860 thousand. Working capital absorbed cash: trade receivables used USD 45,481 thousand and inventories USD 47,321 thousand, and the filing separately reports USD 15.5 million of asbestos-related outflows from discontinued operations inside operating cash flow. The mechanism is that integration costs and working capital growth are absorbing cash just as interest costs rise.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C6
### Liquidity adequacy

Liquidity at October 2, 2026 was cash of USD 188,648 thousand plus USD 760 million of revolver availability, which equals the USD 1,050 million facility less USD 290 million drawn and is available only while financial covenants are met. Of the cash, USD 176.5 million sat outside the United States, where repatriation can bear withholding taxes and minority-owner restrictions, so the usable domestic cash is small. Debt due within a year is USD 9,357 thousand, the nearest large maturities are the notes due April 2029 and the term loan and revolver due October 2030, and the revolver carries a springing maturity whose trigger the filing does not describe. Letters of credit of USD 53.6 million are outstanding under separate facilities with USD 116.8 million of capacity. The consequence is ample near-term liquidity but a dependence on the revolver, whose covenants cannot be tested from the filings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C7
### Data-quality and definition risks

Three definitions need care. First, ESAB states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA here is operating income plus the cash flow statement's depreciation, amortization and other impairment charges, and it sits USD 123.606 million below the issuer's last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 589.7 million; the gap is restructuring, acquisition and integration costs, inventory step-up and a non-cash option award that the issuer adds back, and the reported measure is the primary denominator here with the adjusted measure shown beside it. Second, carrying value of debt differs from principal by USD 17.972 million of unamortized deferred financing fees at October 2, 2026. Third, the 2025 annual report re-presents the FY2024 cash flow statement, splitting the gain on sale of property from other operating items and issuance costs from other financing, with unchanged totals; the FY2024 column here uses the later presentation.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2024-12-31_esab-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78; calculation C1; calculation C8

The perimeter changes within the sample: Eddyfi contributed net sales of USD 84.3 million in the nine months of 2026 and is in the balance sheet from June 1, 2026, while the 2025 comparatives exclude it. Year-end 2025 debt, cash and the FY2025 ladder therefore describe a smaller group, and no table here blends them with the later balance sheets. No material non-debt funding float was found: contract liabilities were USD 19.7 million at year-end 2025 against USD 26.4 million a year earlier, they sit in accrued liabilities, and no supplier-finance or factoring programme is described.
### Subsequent events and multi-figure events

Three events after the balance sheet date are kept out of period figures. A common stock dividend of USD 7.5 million was paid on October 16, 2026 and the preferred stock dividend of USD 2.8 million on October 15, 2026, each of which was already accrued and lifts net debt when paid; in October 2026 the company settled all remaining obligations under its US pension plan and expects a non-cash charge of about USD 37 million in the fourth quarter, with no cash effect stated. The post-balance-sheet table shows the net debt effect of the two dividends.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C9

The Eddyfi price is a multi-figure event: about USD 1.45 billion at signing, about USD 1.5 billion of consideration net of cash received at closing, USD 1,487,883 thousand in the allocation before USD 24,673 thousand of cash acquired, and a nine-month acquisitions outflow of USD 1,469,372 thousand that covers all acquisitions. The cash flow figure serves cash paid and the allocation serves balance sheet purchase accounting; the definition register keeps all four.

## Gaps

- No pro forma or Eddyfi stand-alone EBITDA is printed for the enlarged business, so leverage at April 3, July 3 and October 2, 2026 puts the full acquisition debt over last-twelve-months EBITDA that holds about 4 months of Eddyfi at most; it restricts any statement of run-rate leverage. Severity: High. Action: obtain the acquisition-date presentation or an earnings release with pro forma EBITDA, or show leverage on both bases.

- Covenant levels, the credit agreement's EBITDA definition and the springing-maturity condition are not printed, although compliance at every date is stated; covenant headroom is not calculable for any period. Severity: High. Action: obtain the amended and restated credit agreement.

- No debt maturity ladder after the 2026 financing is printed; the only ladder is at December 31, 2025 and omits the 2031 senior notes and the 2026 revolver draw, so the maturity chart shows a pre-acquisition wall. Severity: Medium. Action: assemble the ladder from the instrument terms in the debt note and label it as derived.

- Cash interest paid is not printed in the quarterly reports, so EBITDA cover is calculable for FY2024 and FY2025 only and not after the 2026 financing. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain cash paid for interest for the nine months of 2026 or state cover on interest expense with that definition labelled.

- The legal rank and security of the term loan and revolver, and their rank against the senior notes, are not stated, so no debt stack is drawn and the instrument register shows security and ranking as not supplied for those facilities. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreement and indentures.

- Cash flow statements are year-to-date only, so discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows and the fourth quarter of 2025 are not reported; Q4 2025 net sales are derived by difference, the second-quarter income columns are not tabulated because they are carried in the six-month columns, and cash flows by quarter would be derived and labelled. Severity: Low. Action: derive and label when a quarterly view is needed.

- Per-share lines, the statement of comprehensive income and the statement of equity are not tabulated, and the FY2023 and FY2022 columns of the annual reports are not carried; they do not affect leverage, cover or liquidity. Severity: Low. Action: extend the tables if earnings per share or a longer history is needed.

- Instrument carrying values are not disclosed, the other debt line of 7041 thousand is not described, and no floor or amortisation schedule is stated for the term loan after 2026. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement; meanwhile the register carries principal and one financing cost adjustment row.

- Several statement lines print a dash for a period (pension settlement loss, preferred stock proceeds and dividends, term loan lines, Senior Notes proceeds); each is recorded as not supplied rather than as zero. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the credit view.
- No operating KPIs such as orders, backlog or volumes are stated beyond the issuer's margins and sales growth components. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a volume view is wanted.

- The Q1 2026 balance sheet holds cash raised ahead of the Eddyfi closing, so its net debt is not comparable with year-end 2025 or the later dates; it is shown with that label and not treated as a leverage reading. Severity: Low. Action: none; read the July 3 and October 2, 2026 rows as the first post-closing figures.

## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

ESAB has no sponsor, and insiders took USD 125.0 million of the Eddyfi equity on the same terms as outsiders, so governance risk is moderate; the exposure is financial policy, since equity funded only 21.73% of the price. Creditors should watch whether further acquisitions or dividend increases come before the balance sheet is repaired.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation A1; calculation A2

The business is consumables-led, with consumables at 60.96% of nine-month net sales and 60.40% of sales in EMEA & APAC, about 5% in Russia and an acquired inspection business that raises the equipment share. Board composition, ownership percentages and pay are not in the supplied filings, and the chief financial officer and chief accounting officer both changed in 2026, so governance conclusions rest on disclosed actions rather than structure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation A5; calculation A7
### Key findings

- **No sponsor controls ESAB, but one holder group matters.** The company has been listed since April 2022 and the 2025 annual report names Mitchell P. Rales and Steven M. Rales as holders with registration rights; the 2026 quarterly report calls Mitchell Rales the Executive Chair. Their percentage holding is not stated, so the weight of this group cannot be measured. The consequence is that value extraction by a controlling owner is not documented, but neither can it be ruled out from the filings.

- **Insiders supported the Eddyfi financing rather than extracting from it.** Entities affiliated with Mitchell Rales bought USD 100.0 million and entities affiliated with Steven Rales USD 25.0 million of the USD 175.0 million of 6.50% preferred stock, 71.43% of the issue, on the terms agreed with unaffiliated investors, and USD 143 million of common stock went to institutions at USD 114.00 a share. Together the placements equal 21.73% of the net consideration, so about four fifths of the price was met from cash, new notes and the revolver. The preferred stock adds a cash dividend of USD 11,375 thousand a year ahead of common dividends and below all debt.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A3

- **Financial policy is acquisitive and has not yet turned to repair.** The company completed four acquisitions in 2025 for USD 452,374 thousand of consideration and Eddyfi in June 2026, the quarterly dividend was raised from USD 0.10 to USD 0.12 a share, a rise of 20.00%, while debt was rising, and the share repurchase authority has never been used. Using equity for part of the price and leaving buybacks idle is creditor-friendly; raising the dividend at the closing is not.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation A9

- **Senior-team turnover coincides with integration.** The chief financial officer named in the 2025 annual report was replaced, with the chief executive acting as interim principal financial officer on May 7, 2026 and a new chief financial officer signing from August 6, 2026; the chief accounting officer also changed, and the head of Fabrication Technology resigned effective about May 31, 2026. The filings give no reason, so the creditor risk is execution on a USD 1.5 billion integration with a largely new finance team and an unexplained departure.

- **Management is paid for equity value, not credit metrics.** Performance options were granted on June 10 and July 1, 2026 at exercise prices of USD 82.92 and USD 93.69 a share, vesting only if the share price reaches USD 140.00, USD 170.00 and USD 200.00, with a grant-date value of USD 64.4 million; the issuer excludes the related expense from Adjusted EBITDA. The incentive favours growth and acquisitions, and no creditor metric appears in the disclosed terms.

- **Revenue is resilient but exposed to tariffs, Russia and the Middle East.** Consumables were 65.81% of FY2025 net sales and 60.96% in the nine months of 2026, which gives recurring demand, while equipment rose to 42.51% of Q3 2026 sales from 34.34% a year earlier as Eddyfi's inspection equipment arrived. Russia is about 5% of net sales with about USD 51 million of cash that may be hard to withdraw, and the war in Iran and the closing of the Strait of Hormuz cut sales in the Middle East.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation A5

- **A legacy asbestos liability sits in discontinued operations.** Net of insurance, the asbestos liability is USD 53,143 thousand, with more claims filed in the nine months of 2026 than a year earlier, and cash outflows of USD 15.5 million in the nine months; it is long-dated and uncapped beyond 15 years, so it competes with debt service for cash over time.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation A8
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a moderate governance rating is the pace and direction of financial policy: ESAB bought four businesses in 2025 and a USD 1.5 billion business in 2026, raised its dividend as the deal closed, and granted management options that pay only on a much higher share price, all while its finance leadership changed and one acquired unit's controls were still being brought into scope at the end of 2025. Insider participation in the preferred stock can also be read the other way, since the Rales-affiliated buyers took a 6.50% cumulative claim that ranks ahead of common equity and the placement terms were negotiated with the unaffiliated investors rather than set by the company alone. The view would move to high if a further large acquisition were funded mainly with debt before leverage falls, if the dividend rose again, or if the missing proxy statement showed a small board majority tied to the Rales Holders. It would move to low if the proxy statement showed an independent board and no concentrated holder, the credit agreement showed distribution limits that bind, and the reason for the finance leadership change proved routine.
### Limitations

- Ownership percentages and the Rales Holders' stake are not stated, so the conclusion that no controlling holder is extracting value cannot be tested and stays a statement about documented actions only.
- Directors' independence, committees and pay sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the moderate governance rating is provisional and could move either way once board structure is known.

- No credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so what distributions, acquisitions and debt incurrence the documents permit is not established; the financial-policy conclusion rests on what ESAB has done, not on what it may do.
- The reasons for the 2026 finance and Fabrication Technology leadership changes are not stated, so the finding on integration execution risk could be too cautious if the changes were planned.

- Eddyfi's stand-alone results and margins are not supplied beyond its sales contribution, so the statement that the acquisition raises the equipment share and adds inspection technology is not matched by any view of its profitability.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction is the acquisition of Eddyfi Holding Inc., a Québec-incorporated inspection and monitoring technology business. ESAB signed the share purchase agreement on January 31, 2026 at about USD 1.45 billion, completed it on June 1, 2026, and reports consideration of about USD 1.5 billion net of cash received, with goodwill of USD 811.2 million and intangibles of USD 752.0 million on a preliminary allocation that can still change within a year. Eddyfi's 2025 revenue was about USD 240 million.

The financing combined cash on hand, a USD 1.0 billion issue of senior notes due 2031 on March 26, 2026, a revolver draw, USD 175.0 million of 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred stock and USD 143 million of common stock placed with institutions at USD 114.00 a share. The notes carry a special mandatory redemption if the acquisition had not closed, USD 240 million of their proceeds repaid the revolver first, and a USD 1.0 billion bridge commitment from JPMorgan Chase signed on January 31, 2026 was never drawn and was terminated on March 26, 2026 after USD 4.8 million of fees. Insiders affiliated with the Executive Chair and his brother bought USD 100.0 million and USD 25.0 million of the preferred stock.

The existing debt stack before the deal was a USD 350 million term loan A and a USD 1.05 billion revolver under an amended and restated credit agreement dated October 16, 2025, both due October 16, 2030 with a springing maturity under circumstances the filings do not describe, and USD 700 million of senior notes due April 15, 2029 issued on April 9, 2024. After the deal the senior notes total USD 1,700 million at October 2, 2026, with USD 290 million drawn on the revolver and USD 760 million available. Certain US subsidiaries guarantee the credit agreement and the senior notes.

Earlier transactions set the pattern: four acquisitions in 2025 (Bavaria on April 30, DeltaP on June 4, Aktiv on July 9 and EWM on August 22) for USD 452,374 thousand of preliminary consideration, and Sager and ESAB Bangladesh in 2024. In October 2026 the company settled the remaining obligations of its US pension plan and expects a non-cash charge of about USD 37 million in the fourth quarter. The filings state no other new debt issue after October 2, 2026.

## Request

## Findings
### Bottom line

ESAB's fundamental credit profile is adequate but stretched by acquisition debt, with total debt at 5.00x reported and 3.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, so creditors rely on integration and cash flow, not balance-sheet cushion, until leverage falls. Cash of USD 188,648 thousand (pro forma cash is not established), USD 760 million undrawn on the revolver, no large maturity before April 2029 and consumables at 60.96% of nine-month sales are the main supports; an estimated interest cover of 3.69x, down from 7.46x in FY2025, a raised dividend and finance leadership turnover are the main constraints.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation B1; calculation B8; calculation B9

The primary downside path is an earnings or working-capital shortfall during integration that leaves cash flow after capital spending too thin to cut debt, while the revolver covenants, which are not disclosed, govern the one liquidity backstop. This is not a rating and not a view on any security.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Key findings

- **The business profile is the strongest dimension.** Consumables were 60.96% of nine-month net sales, about 80% of FY2025 sales came from outside the United States, and sales split 39.60% Americas and 60.40% EMEA & APAC, so no region or product group dominates; issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 19.03% of last-twelve-months net sales. The consequence is revenue that is recurring and spread, which supports cash flow through a downturn better than a project-driven equipment business would.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B4; calculation B10

- **Leverage is the weakest dimension and is driven by the acquisition.** Total debt is 5.00x reported and 3.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA at October 2, 2026, against 2.49x and 2.21x at year-end 2025, which is before Eddyfi, so a pro forma year-end 2025 figure is not established. Net leverage is 4.59x reported and 3.63x adjusted; pro forma for the USD 7.5 million common dividend paid on 2026-10-16 it is 4.61x, and for the USD 2.8 million preferred dividend paid on 2026-10-15 it is 4.60x. Last-twelve-months EBITDA holds only about 4 months of Eddyfi, so the run-rate ratio is lower than these figures, but the filings do not say by how much.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1; calculation B2

- **Liquidity is adequate and maturities are back-ended.** Cash is USD 188,648 thousand and USD 760 million of the USD 1,050 million revolver is undrawn, with 27.62% drawn; the first large maturity is USD 700 million of senior notes in April 2029, followed by the term loan and revolver in October 2030 and USD 1,000 million of notes in April 2031, so the two bonds are 72.43% of principal. Pro forma cash for the October 2026 dividends is not established. The consequence is no refinancing pressure for more than two years, but a concentrated wall from 2029 to 2031 that needs market access.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; calculation B7; calculation B8

- **Cash generation is positive but thin against the debt.** Last-twelve-months cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 180,737 thousand, which is 7.76% of total debt, and USD 153,565 thousand after cash dividends; nine-month operating cash flow fell to USD 153,017 thousand from USD 163,514 thousand as integration, restructuring and working capital absorbed cash. At this rate deleveraging from cash flow alone is slow, so it depends on earnings growth from Eddyfi and the margin programmes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B6

- **Interest cost is the main step-up and cover will fall.** Cash interest paid was USD 66,569 thousand in FY2025 for cover of 7.46x on reported EBITDA, but the larger debt at a weighted-average rate of 5.40% implies roughly USD 126,360 thousand a year, an estimated cover of 3.69x on reported EBITDA and 4.67x on adjusted EBITDA. This is an estimate, not cash paid, because the quarterly reports do not print interest paid; the consequence is that fixed charges absorb a much larger share of EBITDA than the FY2025 ratio suggests.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B3; calculation B9

- **Financial policy and governance are mixed and rated moderate.** Equity funded 21.73% of the Eddyfi price and insiders took 71.43% of the preferred stock, which is supportive, but the quarterly dividend was raised 20.00% while debt rose, the finance leadership changed during the integration, and board and ownership detail is not supplied. The consequence is that the equity cushion is real but the pace of repair depends on choices the filings do not constrain.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B10

- **Legacy and external exposures press on the view without changing it.** Net asbestos exposure is USD 53,143 thousand with USD 15.5 million of nine-month outflows, Russia is about 5% of net sales, and tariffs and the war in Iran weigh on margins and Middle East sales. These compete for cash with debt service but are small against cash flow and are already in the reported results.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that leverage is less of a concern than it looks is that the debt is fully loaded but the earnings are not: last-twelve-months issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 589.7 million holds only about 4 months of Eddyfi, whose 2025 revenue of about USD 240 million was 8.44% of ESAB's net sales, so a full year would lift EBITDA and lower leverage, and liquidity of USD 760 million undrawn plus cash gives time. The case that it is worse than it looks is that reported EBITDA is USD 466,094 thousand, well below the adjusted figure, because restructuring and acquisition costs are real cash, and that the estimate of cover at 3.69x leaves little room if earnings slip. The view would improve if a pro forma EBITDA showed total leverage below 4x, if cash flow after capital spending rose above 10% of debt, or if the credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would worsen if reported EBITDA fell again, if the dividend rose or another large acquisition were debt-funded before leverage falls, or if the unexplained finance leadership change proved a sign of control problems.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation B4; calculation B9
### Limitations

- Covenant levels and definitions are not supplied, so the conclusion that liquidity is adequate holds only while the revolver stays available; if a covenant binds at current leverage, the USD 760 million of availability could shrink and the view on liquidity would weaken.

- The cover of 3.69x is an estimate from the weighted-average rate and principal, not interest paid, so the conclusion that fixed charges absorb much more of EBITDA could be too severe or too mild by the effect of swaps, timing and the new debt's actual cost.
- No management guidance, forecast or pro forma EBITDA was supplied, so the outlook and the downside scenario are qualitative and the size of the leverage overstatement cannot be put into the view.
- No agency rating, bond price or peer data was supplied, so the statement that refinancing access is adequate rests on the maturity profile and liquidity alone and not on market signals.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. A global, diversified, consumables-led business with about 80% of sales outside the United States and no customer above 10% of trade receivables turns volume into recurring cash flow, which supports debt service through a cycle. Liquidity of cash plus an undrawn USD 1,050 million revolver covers near-term needs, and nothing large matures before April 2029. Insiders and institutions put in USD 318 million of equity, which limited the debt added. The cash flow chain is evidence from the revenue and debt notes, the mechanism of recurring revenue and a back-ended maturity profile, and the implication of lower refinancing and default risk in the next two years.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weaknesses. Debt has roughly doubled to 5.00x reported EBITDA against 2.49x at year-end 2025, interest cost will take a much larger share of EBITDA, cash flow after capital spending is only 7.76% of debt, and a dividend raise, option awards tied to share prices and unexplained finance leadership changes point to a policy that favours growth over repair. The mechanism is higher fixed charges and slower deleveraging, and the implication is greater sensitivity of default and refinancing risk to an earnings miss during the integration year.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B9

### Company description and ownership

ESAB makes welding and cutting systems, consumables, gas control equipment, automation and robotics, software and, since June 2026, advanced inspection technology, selling through distributors and direct sales in about 150 countries. Consumables are the larger and steadier part of sales, equipment the cyclical part, and acquisitions are a core strategy: four in 2025 and Eddyfi in 2026. The credit linkage is that recurring consumables and global spread support cash flow and refinancing confidence, while a strategy built on acquisitions means leverage will recur as a risk unless funding stays equity-light. ESAB is a listed company without a sponsor; Mitchell P. Rales is Executive Chair and the Rales Holders hold registration rights, but their percentage is not stated, so ownership concentration and distribution behaviour are rated on actions, not structure.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 23
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Consumables, which are replaced as they are used, were 65.81% of FY2025 sales and 60.96% of nine-month 2026 sales, so volume follows industrial activity but with a floor from maintenance and replacement demand. Pricing has helped: Americas net sales from existing businesses rose on USD 25.2 million of customer pricing in the nine months while volumes fell in South America and Mexico, and EMEA & APAC organic growth was supported by pricing and Asia volumes against Middle East weakness. Organic growth was 0.9% in the nine months after minus 1.1% in FY2025, so revenue is stable rather than growing and acquisitions supply most of the growth; the credit implication is steady but not expanding cash flow that cannot by itself deleverage quickly.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Steel, iron, copper and aluminum are the main inputs, tariffs added cost from April 2025, and gross margin fell from 37.9% in FY2024 to 36.9% in FY2025 before recovering to 38.1% in the nine months of 2026 as pricing, favourable tariff effects and acquisitions helped. Operating income margin fell as selling and administrative costs and restructuring rose with the larger group, so the issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.8% for nine months is below 19.7% for FY2025. Margins can be defended through pricing, as 2026 shows, but integration and restructuring costs are cash, so reported EBITDA is the better measure of what services debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital spending is modest at USD 49,700 thousand in nine months of 2026, though it rose from USD 27,654 thousand, and the issuer separates asbestos and restructuring cash from capital spending. Conversion of reported EBITDA to cash flow after capital spending was 38.78% over the last twelve months, held down by restructuring, integration, working capital and interest, and cash taxes and interest were substantial. The implication is that EBITDA overstates what is available for debt service, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA rising and cash costs falling, not on capital spending cuts.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5
### Market frameworks, credit-translated

Rivalry is the force that matters: the filing names Lincoln Electric and the welding business of Illinois Tool Works as competitors and describes a fragmented market where price, quality and delivery decide, which caps pricing power and implies margins are defended by brands and aftermarket support rather than by dominance. Buyer power is limited by a diversified customer base with no customer above 10% of receivables, supplier power by multiple sources for steel, copper and aluminum, and entry and substitution threats are low in consumables and rising in automation, where the company itself invests in software and robotics. Macro, tariff and war factors are material enough for a PEST view: US tariffs raised costs and prices, IEEPA tariff refunds are not yet recorded as receivables, the Middle East conflict cut sales, and sanctions leave about USD 51 million of Russian cash hard to withdraw; the credit consequence is cost and cash volatility that the company has so far passed through to prices.

In credit terms the strengths are scale and spread, recurring consumables, pricing power in 2026, a back-ended maturity profile and insider equity support; the weaknesses are acquisition leverage, a rising interest burden, thin cash flow against debt, and unexplained leadership changes; the opportunities are Eddyfi earnings and synergies, tariff refunds and margin programmes; and the threats are an earnings miss during integration, trade and geopolitical shocks, further debt-funded deals and covenant constraints on the revolver.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

On a ratings-style lens the assessments are as follows. Scale and market position are strong, and competitive advantage and business diversification average to strong given brands, aftermarket and geographic spread. Cost and capex flexibility and margin stability are average: pricing has defended margins but restructuring and integration costs are high. Free cash flow stability is average to weak because conversion is below 40% of reported EBITDA and falling interest cover will bite. Ability to refinance is average, helped by a back-ended wall and equity support but limited by leverage near 5x reported and unknown covenants. Liquidity is average to strong on cash and an undrawn revolver subject to covenants, and financial policy and governance are average because supportive equity funding is offset by a raised dividend, option incentives and turnover. The trend is deterioration in 2026 from the acquisition, with the main missing datapoints being covenant levels, pro forma EBITDA and interest paid.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B5
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are a full year of Eddyfi, pricing, tariff refunds and margin programmes; the headwinds are a high interest bill, continuing restructuring and integration cash costs, weak South American, Mexican and Middle East volumes, and the refinancing step at the 2029 notes. Over three to five years the maturity wall of 2029 to 2031 is the dominant issue and depends on leverage having fallen by then; the structural tailwind is automation, inspection and high-growth markets, which the issuer puts at 52% of FY2025 revenue by its own definition. No management guidance was supplied, so the outlook is qualitative.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esab-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-02_esab-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 47; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Qualitative downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with softer industrial demand and tariff-driven pricing fatigue during the first full year after the deal, the first operational break being lower consumables volumes and integration costs that run longer than planned. Reported EBITDA, already USD 466,094 thousand over twelve months, would fall, working capital would absorb cash again as in the nine months of 2026, and cash flow after capital spending, now USD 180,737 thousand, would approach the cash dividends and fixed charges. Liquidity of cash and USD 760 million undrawn would still cover near-term needs, but leverage would rise further and covenant headroom, which is not disclosed, becomes the observable trigger: a tightening revolver would leave the 2029 notes to be refinanced from a weaker position. Management levers are the dividend, capital spending, restructuring and asset sales; the evidence supports resilience sufficient to avoid distress in the next two years but not a comfortable deleveraging path.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B5; calculation B7
### Overall credit view

Overall, ESAB presents a solid business profile supported by scale, a consumables-led and geographically spread revenue base and insider equity support, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition leverage, a much higher interest burden and thin cash flow against debt. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to recurring consumables and pricing, but conversion is held down by integration and restructuring cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on deleveraging before the 2029 notes, on covenant headroom in the revolver and on market access. The primary downside path is an earnings or working-capital shortfall during integration. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, covenant terms, interest paid and management guidance. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: acquisition leverage with an undisclosed covenant backstop.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

This answer corrects one wording in Business & governance: asbestos costs beyond fifteen years are not estimated by the issuer, which is different from the phrase uncapped used there; the net exposure figure is unchanged.
